title: solutions-pro-services-weekly-sync-notes-2026-06-30
content:
Meeting: Solutions Engineering + Pro Services Weekly Sync
Date: 2026-06-30 10:00am PT
Attendees: Aisha (notes/lead), Miguel, Riley, Samir, Jordan, Erin (customer success - partial)
Regrets: Priya
Duration: 45m

Agenda:
- Quick round-robin customer integration statuses (15m)
- Blockers and escalations (10m)
- Capacity / scheduling / HW availability (5m)
- Action items and next steps (10m)

High-level notes / context:
- This week focused on pushing three on-prem deployments (Acme, Atlas Health pilot, FinLedger canary) through network and infra validation. We hit predictable networking delays (VPC peering + customer firewall rules) that cost ~3 business days for Acme; need to bake this into future timelines.
- Reminder: Dedicated infra availability for July is tighter—release-engineering forecast shows limited GPU pool on 7/6-7/10 window. Coordinate with infra to prioritize scheduled canaries.

Customer-by-customer updates:
1) Acme Corp (on-prem, Phase 2)
- Status: final infra validation in progress. Data path tests successful except intermittent TLS renegotiation between customer LB and our agent.
- Current priority: get TLS renegotiation fixed, finish config drift audit, complete runbook handoff to SRE.
- Blockers: customer's ops team requires specific cipher suites; their LB does not support TLS1.3 handshake we default to. Firewall allowed ports but deep-packet inspection propagates latency spikes.
- Tickets: SVC-4123 (TLS + networking), created support PR to infra team for cipher change.
- Action items:
  - Miguel to run packet-capture with Acme ops and share pcap by 2026-07-01.
  - Riley to draft runbook edits for non-TLS1.3 fallback and submit to Confluence by 2026-07-02.
  - Jordan to coordinate SLA acknowledgement doc with legal and send to Acme by 2026-07-03.

2) Atlas Health (private VPC pilot)
- Status: pilot node provisioning completed; model variant testing started with redwood-small/quantized. First end-to-end inference tests succeeded but observed 5–8% higher token latency under 95th percentile than expected.
- Suspected cause: autoscaling cold-starts and slower kernel selection for quantized variant on customer GPU profile.
- Blockers: need SRE + infra help to tune instance warmup and to add pre-warm pods for scheduled workloads.
- Action items:
  - Samir to open SRE run to pre-warm nodes for peak windows; target 2026-07-05.
  - Miguel to run profiling on kv-cache hit rates and share graphs in #solutions-pro-services by 2026-07-02.
  - Customer request: enable ephemeral logs export to their Splunk cluster—Riley to scope work and provide ETA 2026-07-06.

3) FinLedger (hosted -> dedicated migration, canary)
- Status: Canary deployment passed functional tests; performance regression detected vs hosted baseline (3% increase in median latency, 12% in P95).
- Immediate plan: roll back kernel optimizations and re-run microbenchmarks; compare quantization profiles.
- Blockers: limited access to customer's synthetic load generator; support is queued behind other GTM requests.
- Action items:
  - Aisha to coordinate with FinLedger SE on getting synthetic load creds and schedule for 2026-07-01.
  - Samir to run kernel selection comparison and post results to the Confluence canary page by 2026-07-02.

4) EduNext (integration + evals)
- Status: Eval harness built; quality regressions flagged on prompt set 4 (hallucination rate up for long-context summarization).
- Plan: run A/B between current model and a higher-context variant; propose prompt engineering mitigations.
- Action items:
  - Riley to assemble prompt/test deck and hypothesis list by 2026-07-02.
  - Miguel to schedule weekly check-ins with customer PM starting 2026-07-07.

Blockers / escalations (team-wide):
- Infra GPU pool constraints in early July. Product Eng and Release Eng synced; need prioritization matrix for canaries.
- Networking: customers keep hitting obscure firewall/SSL edgecases; propose creating standard network checklist (template) for new on-prem engagements.
- Observability: some customers asked for longer retention on per-route traces—sales asks for pricing impact. Product to surface a formal offering.

Operational notes / helps needed:
- Release window conflicts: Jordan to advocate for rescheduling non-critical canaries to later July to avoid resource contention. (Jordan will update calendar by 2026-07-01).
- New runbook template: Riley to draft network + TLS checklist and share with Solutions + SRE for comment. Target draft 2026-07-02.
- Capacity planning: Samir to publish July GPU allocation spreadsheet (sheet link to be added) by 2026-07-01.

Decisions made:
- For Acme, implement TLS fallback path in runbook and continue investigation; do not delay handoff unless new failures observed.
- For FinLedger canary, pause additional rollouts until microbenchmark parity is within 5% of hosted baseline.

Action items summary (owner — due):
- Miguel: pcap for Acme + profiling graphs for Atlas (2026-07-01, 2026-07-02)
- Riley: runbook edits + prompt/test deck + network checklist draft (2026-07-02, 2026-07-02, 2026-07-02)
- Samir: SRE pre-warm request + kernel comparison + July GPU allocation spreadsheet (2026-07-05, 2026-07-02, 2026-07-01)
- Jordan: SLA/contract coordination and calendar updates (2026-07-03, 2026-07-01)
- Aisha: coordinate FinLedger synthetic load access (2026-07-01)

Open questions:
- Should we add a standard TLS profile matrix to the onboarding checklist for all on-prem customers? (favored yes — need template)
- What is acceptable perf delta for dedicated migrations before we block rollouts? (proposed: 5% median, 10% P95 — needs product sign-off)

Next meeting: 2026-07-07 10:00am PT
Notes prepared by: Aisha Patel
Link to meeting recording: (internal) https://zoom.company/rec/abc123 (placeholder)
